assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a designable chemical reaction: bifunctional degraders and molecular glues (thalidomide-class) reprogram E3 ligases to destroy chosen proteins. A general chemical tool and a new therapeutic modality, which is what I value most.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, the mechanistic anchor for molecular glues. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so a three-person cut leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories, with degraders in clinical trials and mechanisms confirmed structurally. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is not yet established to my knowledge, but the chemistry is mature enough.
uncertainties: Credit split between PROTAC inventors and the molecular-glue/cereblon line may call for different recognition.
I cannot independently verify the current clinical status of degraders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides is nucleotide chemistry at its core, and it transformed biology and medicine. Impact is enormous and the discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry; Rothberg (454, Ion Torrent), Mayer and Ju contributed parallel or alternative chemistries. Allocation across competing platforms is the main difficulty, but a Solexa-based pair is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: two decades of routine global use, with independent confirmation by wide adoption.
uncertainties: Competing contributions from other platforms may be judged equally decisive.
Exact decisive contributions to the reversible-terminator chemistry, from my recollection, are not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base to another (deaminase chemistry) without double-strand breaks, giving precise genome editing with direct therapeutic relevance. Strong chemistry-of-life contribution and a general tool.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention. Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors of the first cytosine and adenine base editors, and Nishida and Kondo reported an independent deaminase-based system. A single-laureate configuration is cleanest but may be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation has started and the method is widely reproduced, though the field is young and long-term safety (off-target deamination, bystander edits) is still being measured, so timing could be early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the CRISPR prize (2020) could affect how the committee views novelty.
Whether the prime-editing entry should be combined with this one is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A RNA methylation, with writers, erasers and readers, adds a chemical regulatory layer to gene expression. It is a clear chemical-modification discovery with links to cancer and development.
assessment.attribution: Dominissini/Rechavi and Meyer/Jaffrey mapped m6A transcriptome-wide; He and Jia identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and framed reversibility. Many contributors, and the seven-name list shows fragmentation of credit.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, but I know of ongoing debate over specific mapping methods, antibody specificity and some functional claims, so interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Quantification disputes (for example m6A versus m6Am and mapping resolution) make me want measurements checked independently.
Credit among He, Jaffrey, Rechavi and Jia is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs incorporate unnatural amino acids in living cells, extending the genetic code and giving biologists a general chemical tool for site-specific protein modification.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang first established the in vivo method; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and multiple codons and to genome recoding; Yokoyama and Mehl also made contributions. Schultz, Chin and Wang is a plausible trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used, with independent confirmation, though therapeutic use is still modest.
uncertainties: Whether Chin's later recoding work needs separate recognition.
Impact is mainly as a tool rather than as a broad change to chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single nucleic-acid molecules electrically and enables long-read sequencing. Original concept and engineered pores are decisive chemistry-meets-biophysics advances.
assessment.attribution: Branton and Deamer proposed and demonstrated DNA translocation in nanopores; Kasianowicz was first author on the key paper; Bayley engineered protein pores; Akeson showed single-base resolution via enzyme control. At most three names is a hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed and reproduced widely, though the story is a long chain with accuracy still improving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson is genuinely contested.
Sequencing may be thought to overlap with the sequencing candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of a mutant cysteine in KRAS G12C turned a long-'undruggable' oncogene into a tractable target, an elegant demonstration of chemistry giving selectivity, and Shokat's chemical-genetic analog-sensitive kinase work was a general tool.
assessment.attribution: Single credited person with clear decisive contributions; clinical drugs built on his tethering discovery were developed by companies, which may raise questions of credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved KRAS G12C drugs provide strong confirmation and clinical validation, so timing is arguably right.
uncertainties: Recognition for the drug-development stage versus the discovery stage is ambiguous.
Single-laureate prizes are rare, so pairing with another entry could be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates explain how cells organize without membranes, a physical-chemistry view of cell compartmentalization with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granules; Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction-driven phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed the theory and physical-chemistry grounding.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing and influential, but I would want more independent quantitative confirmation that observed condensates are functionally phase-separated in cells and not artifacts of overexpression; the field is still contested and arguably premature.
uncertainties: Functional significance in vivo is debated.
Credit among experiment and theory contributors is unclear.
